interface.title: Merrypopins: Nano-indentation Pop-in Detector (Streamlit app)
interface.stage_of_work: Data analysis: preprocessing raw instrument curves, detecting events, computing statistics and exporting results
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a raw Hysitron load-depth indentation curve, clean it and find the contact point, run up to four pop-in detectors and see where they agree, then compute and download load-depth and stress-strain pop-in statistics.

data.note: test_indent.txt was uploaded through the sidebar '📄 Upload indentation .txt' uploader. It parsed to 16390 points, min load 40.42 µN, max load 200206.40 µN, timestamp Mon Jun 06 00:32:13 2025, 16390 declared points. No .tdm/.tdx metadata file was available, so that optional step was skipped. After the first browser crash the screenshot numbering restarted. screens/001–026 come from the second session. screens/027–030 survive from the first session (the same file with the same default settings, which found 216 pop-ins against 215 in the second session). The CNN autoencoder retrains on every run, so counts vary between runs (the replay saw Total 215, Confident ≥2: 3, IFOREST 137 in one run and Total 219, CNN 55 in another). check/screens/* are from the replay agent's session.

features.name: Raw-file parse check with summary metrics
features.general: Upload an instrument export and see a preview table plus key summary numbers, so you know it was read correctly before analysing it
features.specific: The sidebar .txt uploader feeds 'Raw data (head)' (Depth/Load/Time) and 'File info' metrics (Points, Min load µN, Max load µN, Timestamp, Declared points)
steps: Upload the .txt file in the sidebar
Read the first rows of the parsed table
Compare Points with Declared points and check the load range and timestamp
serves_tasks: Load a raw instrument file and confirm it was read correctly

features.name: Preprocessing with raw vs. processed overlay
features.general: Toggle signal-cleaning steps, thresholds and edge-trimming margins and see the raw and cleaned curves overlaid, with the detected onset marked, then export the cleaned data
features.specific: Sidebar checkboxes (Remove data before min(load), Auto-rescale depth, Trim/flag contact point), an Advanced thresholds expander (Baseline points, Noise × k, Smooth window, Poly-order), a Default/Custom/None Mode radio, and Edge trimming controls (Trim first points, Trim margin in points, Ignore after max-load). Results show in the 'Raw vs. Pre-processed' Plotly chart with a Contact marker and in the 'Download CSV of Preprocessed Data' and 'Download PNG' buttons
steps: Pick a preprocessing Mode (Default / Custom / None)
Toggle the cleaning steps and adjust the advanced thresholds
Set the edge-trimming options and margin
Inspect the overlay and the contact-point marker
Download the preprocessed CSV or PNG
serves_tasks: Remove pre-contact noise, rescale and mark the contact point, then compare raw and cleaned curves
Review the advanced cleaning thresholds and edge-trimming settings

features.name: Multi-detector ensemble with agreement count
features.general: Enable several anomaly detectors side by side, each with its own parameters, run them together, and see per-method hit counts plus how many events at least two methods agree on
features.specific: Four columns (Isolation Forest: contamination and stiffness window; CNN Autoencoder: epochs, window, batch, threshold ×σ; Fourier derivative: threshold σ and spacing; Savitzky-Golay: window, poly order, threshold σ, derivative order), each with an Enable checkbox and sliders. '🚀 Run selected detectors' fills the Detections summary (Total pop-ins, Confident ≥2, and hits per method)
steps: Tick the detectors to use
Adjust each detector's sliders
Press Run selected detectors
Read Total, Confident ≥2 and the per-method hit counts
serves_tasks: Run several independent detectors on the same curve
Separate events that several methods agree on from single-method hits

features.general: Plot the curve with event markers coloured by the method that found them, plus a separate marker for consensus events, and export the plot and annotated table
features.specific: 'Merrypopins Popin Detections' Plotly chart (Iforest, Cnn, Fd and Confident legend entries, with a zoom/pan toolbar) above the 'Download CSV' and 'Download PNG' buttons
steps: Look over where the markers fall on the loading curve
Zoom or pan with the Plotly toolbar, or toggle legend entries
Download the annotated CSV or the PNG

features.name: Results bundle export with session configuration
features.general: Download one archive holding the annotated data, the plot and the settings used, so the analysis can be reproduced or reported
features.specific: '📦 ZIP (CSV + plot + config)' button under the detection plot, giving merrypopins_results.zip (389 KB with test_indent.txt)
steps: Run the detectors so the annotated results exist
Press 📦 ZIP (CSV + plot + config)
Save merrypopins_results.zip alongside the raw file
serves_tasks: Download the annotated data and a bundle of results plus settings

features.name: Per-event statistics table with scatter and CSV export
features.general: Turn detected events into a table of per-event measurements, plot two of them against each other, and export the table and plot
features.specific: Load-Depth Pop-in Statistics (depth_jump, popin_length, with a 'Depth Jump vs Pop-in Length' scatter) and Stress-Strain Pop-in Statistics (stress_jump, strain_jump, stress_slope, strain_slope, with a 'Stress Jump vs Strain Jump' scatter). Sidebar inputs control them: time windows before/after pop-in, min load for stress-strain, Smooth stress, and Remove rows with all NaN. Each section has CSV and plot download buttons. Known issue with test_indent.txt: the load-depth table showed all-None rows despite NaN-row removal being ticked
steps: Set the before/after time windows and the min load in the sidebar
Choose whether to smooth stress and drop all-NaN rows
Read the per-event table (check for all-None rows)
Inspect the scatter of jump vs length or slope
Download the statistics CSV or plot
